clue.text: Ice-cream's eaten by counter before getting pair of stockings and smart dress

indicators.note: eaten signals one piece swallowed inside another

parts.note: a sundae is an ice-cream dish topped with syrup and fruit

indicators.note: counter means running the opposite way, so the little word by is read backwards
pair of takes just the opening two letters of the word stockings

explanation.surface: Someone gobbles a sundae at a shop counter before buying stockings and a smart outfit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'counter' reverses the little word by; 'eaten' puts it inside the ice-cream, and 'before getting' sets the stockings pair after. The surface's shop counter is a decoy.
explanation.definitionFit: Your best clothes, kept for churchgoing, are smart dress worn on special occasions.

clue.text: Heads of state attending conference kindled fire

indicators.note: heads of takes the initial letter of each of the four following words

explanation.surface: Leaders of a country go to a summit where tempers were inflamed.
explanation.definitionFit: To fire someone is to dismiss them from a job, informally to give them the boot.

clue.text: Specification in whisky order or in apple-pie order

definitions.meaning: ordering a whisky without water or ice, you ask for it straight
apple-pie order is perfect tidiness, so everything is trim and orderly

explanation.definitionFit: Undiluted spirits are served neat, and a tidy room is also called that word.

clue.text: Wrist mangler is out of order in a trial of strength

indicators.note: out of order says the letters are jumbled from their proper sequence

explanation.surface: A machine that crushes wrists has broken down during a strength test.
explanation.definitionFit: The bar-room contest of forcing an opponent's hand down onto the table is a strength test.

clue.text: Broker initially taking responsibility for extra dividend

indicators.note: initially takes the opening letter of the word Broker

parts.note: an onus is a burden of responsibility or duty

explanation.surface: A stockbroker first accepts liability for paying an additional dividend.
explanation.definitionFit: An extra payment to shareholders on top of the usual dividend is a special share distribution.

clue.text: Movie trailers seen by Labour politician?

parts.note: Jack Straw was a senior Labour Party minister in Britain
to dog someone is to trail them, so dogs are things that follow behind

explanation.surface: Film previews are watched by a member of the Labour Party.
explanation.walkthrough: 'trailers' looks like film previews but means followers; Jack Straw was British Home Secretary and Foreign Secretary under Tony Blair.
explanation.definitionFit: Sam Peckinpah's 1971 thriller starring Dustin Hoffman is the film named here.

clue.text: Blue jacket for cold fish

indicators.note: a jacket wraps around, so one piece is placed outside the other

parts.note: feeling blue means being sad or low
C is the standard abbreviation for cold on taps

explanation.surface: A sailor's jacket meant for a chilly fish.
explanation.definitionFit: The scad is a type of horse mackerel, a small sea fish.

clue.text: Peninsular county — and islands in general

parts.note: Cornwall is the English county on the south-western peninsula
IS is the usual abbreviation for islands, as on maps

explanation.surface: A survey describing a peninsula county together with islands in broad terms.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in general' reads as 'broadly', but general is the definition: Charles Cornwallis was the British commander who surrendered at Yorktown in 1781.
explanation.definitionFit: Lord Cornwallis was a British army officer of high rank in the American War of Independence.

clue.text: Jumble sorted for a grandsire

indicators.note: sorted suggests the letters are rearranged into a new order

explanation.surface: Muddled jumble tidied up for an old grandfather.
explanation.definitionFit: To jumble things is to throw them out of order, messing up their arrangement.

clue.text: Censor mail distributed by fuel suppliers

indicators.note: distributed means spread around, so these letters are scattered into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: Letters are censored as they are delivered by men who supply fuel.
explanation.definitionFit: Pitmen digging out coal produced the fuel that heated homes and powered industry.

clue.text: The flower of Fair Isle

indicators.note: of here means taken from within, so the letters sit inside the two words Fair Isle

explanation.surface: The prettiest bloom growing on a remote Shetland island.
explanation.walkthrough: Fair Isle is a small island in Shetland, known for its knitwear patterns.
explanation.definitionFit: A plant with sword-shaped leaves and showy blooms, named after the Greek goddess of the rainbow.

clue.text: "Legal Ward"- novel by expert writer of crime stories

indicators.note: novel means new or different, so these letters take a fresh order

parts.note: an ace is an expert, a highly skilled performer

explanation.surface: A novel called 'Legal Ward' written by an expert crime author.
explanation.walkthrough: 'novel' reads as a book but signals rearranging LEGAL WARD into EDGAR WALL.
explanation.definitionFit: This British author wrote scores of thrillers and detective novels and co-created King Kong.

clue.text: I'm separated from my wife so I grew sward for recreation

indicators.note: recreation read as re-creation means remaking, so these letters are rebuilt in another order

explanation.surface: A man explains he lives apart from his wife, so took up growing lawns as a hobby.
explanation.definitionFit: A man whose wife is away for a long time, left alone, is described by this phrase.

clue.text: Unappetising quality of nuts son digests

indicators.note: nuts means crazy, so these letters are jumbled madly

explanation.surface: What makes food unpleasant is whatever crazy dish the boy is digesting.
explanation.definitionFit: Heavy, starchy food that sits in the stomach has this dull, stodgy character.

clue.text: Cheap music provided by girl?

parts.note: a catch is a round for several voices, a piece of music
Penny is a girl's name

explanation.surface: Inexpensive songs supplied by a young woman.
explanation.definitionFit: Something made merely to sell quickly, flashy but worthless, is tawdry or cheap.

clue.text: Poor stationer scolds vigorously

indicators.note: poor suggests something done badly, so these letters are put in a sorry jumble

explanation.surface: A stationer with bad service gets a fierce telling-off.
explanation.definitionFit: To lay into someone verbally is to attack or berate them harshly.

clue.text: D-d-done in one's sleep?

parts.note: the stammered word holds the word done with two extra Ds, and a mixed-up version of a word for dozed off spells it, hinting at slipping into sleep

explanation.walkthrough: D, D and DONE are the letters of NODDED, and 'off' can signal those letters jumbled, so the stutter is a NODDED gone off.
explanation.definitionFit: To drop into sleep while sitting, head drooping, is to doze off unintentionally.

clue.text: It's quite round, a Scottish town

parts.note: quite in the sense of completely, entirely, gives all
the letter O is a round shape

explanation.surface: A Scottish town described as almost circular.
explanation.walkthrough: Alloa is a town in Clackmannanshire, central Scotland.
explanation.definitionFit: Alloa is a town on the River Forth in central Scotland.

clue.text: Double frame for coroneted head of a peer

indicators.note: a frame goes around a picture, so one piece encloses another

parts.note: dual means double, twofold

indicators.note: head picks out the initial letter of the word coroneted

explanation.surface: A double picture frame for a portrait of a lord's crowned head.
explanation.definitionFit: Ducal means relating to a duke, the highest rank of the British peerage.

clue.text: Repudiating plant and eating out

indicators.note: out here means outside, so the eating word wraps around the planting word

parts.note: dining means eating a meal
to sow is to plant seeds

explanation.surface: Turning down gardening and restaurant meals.
explanation.walkthrough: 'eating out' looks like one phrase for restaurant meals; split it, and 'out' becomes the signal for the eating word to sit around the planting word.
explanation.definitionFit: Disowning a person or statement is rejecting it and refusing to acknowledge it any longer.

clue.text: That can't be weighed? I can weigh the pros and cons internally

indicators.note: internally means placed within, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: I can is the same as I am able, shortened to I'm able
to ponder is to think over carefully, weighing up arguments

explanation.surface: Something unweighable, says one who can mull over arguments in their head.
explanation.walkthrough: 'weigh' in the definition is literal; IMPONDERABLE things cannot be weighed, hence the question mark.
explanation.definitionFit: An imponderable is something whose effect cannot be estimated, figuratively incapable of being weighed.

clue.text: Wide awake right after drink

indicators.note: after places the right piece following the drink piece

parts.note: ale is a type of beer, a drink

explanation.surface: Fully conscious after a drink, rightly.
explanation.definitionFit: Being alert means fully watchful and quick to notice, awake and attentive.

clue.text: Emperor clad in cotton

indicators.note: clad in means dressed within, so the letters lie inside the word cotton

explanation.surface: A ruler dressed in plain cotton.
explanation.definitionFit: Otto was the name of several Holy Roman Emperors, beginning with Otto the Great.

clue.text: Leaves seen by king in wood

parts.note: tea consists of dried leaves
K is the abbreviation for king in chess and cards

explanation.surface: Foliage spotted by a monarch in a forest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wood' looks like a forest setting, but it is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Teak is a hard, durable timber from a tropical Asian tree.

clue.text: Mount held back by Tam o'Shanter

indicators.note: back says those contained letters are read in reverse
held means contained, so the letters lie inside Tam o'Shanter

explanation.surface: A climber's mount kept behind by the hero of Burns's poem.
explanation.walkthrough: Tam o'Shanter is the drunken rider of Robert Burns's poem, and a Scots bonnet; the hidden run ANTE is turned back.
explanation.definitionFit: Etna is a volcanic mountain in Sicily, and Mount is often prefixed to its name.

clue.text: Divine loose covers for the crew's quarters

parts.note: to divine is to foresee or predict

indicators.note: covers takes the outside letters of the word loose, its first and last letters

explanation.surface: A fortune teller predicts loose covers for the sailors' cabins.
explanation.walkthrough: 'loose covers' reads as sofa slipcovers, but 'covers' takes the first and last letters of loose.
explanation.definitionFit: The forecastle is the forward part of a ship where sailors traditionally had their berths.

clue.text: Hurdles reported in river one is late to cross

definitions.text: river one is late to cross

indicators.note: reported means spoken of, so the word is heard rather than written

parts.note: in horse racing slang, sticks are the hurdles or fences jumped

explanation.surface: Jumping fences as reported in the river.
explanation.walkthrough: 'late' means dead: in Greek myth the dead are ferried across the Styx into the underworld.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek myth the departed must be ferried over this underworld river by Charon.

clue.text: Out of difficulty in Dutch waters?

definitions.meaning: free of trouble or obligation, released from a predicament
sailing just offshore from the Hook of Holland, a Dutch headland

explanation.definitionFit: Being let go from blame or trouble is escaping a fix, like a fish freed from a line.
